events.title: Hack Night: Web Exploitation 101
events.summary: Hands-on intro to the OWASP Top 10. Break a deliberately vulnerable app, then patch it.
events.description:
Bring your laptop — we'll hack a deliberately vulnerable web app together.

**You'll learn**
- How SQL injection, XSS and CSRF actually work
- Using Burp Suite to intercept and modify requests
- Writing the fix, not just the exploit

**Prerequisites:** a laptop with a modern browser. We'll share a lab VM on the day.

All hacking happens only on lab targets we own. Attacking systems without permission is illegal and against the ISSA code of conduct.

events.title: Cyber Quiz Night
events.summary: A live, Kahoot-style quiz on security, networks and tech trivia. Fastest correct answers win.
events.description:
Play live from your phone while questions appear on the big screen.

- 8 questions, 20 seconds each
- Faster correct answers earn more points (up to 1,000 per question)
- Top 3 win swag and a podium badge on their ISSA profile

Sign in before the quiz starts so you can join the lobby instantly.

events.title: BuildSec Hackathon 2026
events.summary: 36 hours to build secure-by-design software for campus problems. Teams of up to four.
events.description:
Tracks: **Campus Safety**, **Privacy Tech** and **Open Innovation**.

- Teams of 1–4; register individually and enter the same team name
- Submit your repository, a short demo video link and a pitch deck before the deadline
- Judging: impact (30%), security (30%), technical depth (25%), presentation (15%)

Mentors from the core team will be around all night. Food is on us.
events.submission_guidelines: Submit once per team (from any one member's account) with your team name. Include a public repository link and optionally a demo link. You may upload a single .zip, .pdf or .pptx up to 10 MB (link larger files from Drive or GitHub). You can update your submission until the deadline.

events.title: ISSA CTF 2026
events.summary: Our flagship 24-hour jeopardy-style capture-the-flag. Web, pwn, crypto, forensics and OSINT.
events.description:
Compete solo or in teams of up to three. Challenges range from beginner to brutal.

**Members only** — sign up with your college email to be auto-verified as a member.

Flag format: `issa{...}`. Sharing flags between teams leads to disqualification.

quizzes.title: Cyber Quiz Night — Live
quizzes.description: Hosted live at Cyber Quiz Night. Join the lobby and wait for the host to start.

questions.prompt: Which TCP port does HTTPS use by default?
questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS, served on TCP port 443 by default.

questions.prompt: Which attack tricks a logged-in user's browser into sending an unwanted request to a trusted site?
questions.explanation: Cross-Site Request Forgery rides on the victim's existing session. Anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies defend against it.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a hash function rather than an encryption algorithm?
questions.explanation: SHA-256 is a one-way hash. AES and ChaCha20 are symmetric ciphers; RSA is asymmetric.

questions.prompt: In the CIA triad, what does the “I” stand for?
Which tool is best known for network port scanning?
questions.explanation: Nmap discovers hosts and services. Wireshark captures packets, Burp proxies web traffic, John cracks passwords.

questions.prompt: What does adding a unique salt to each password hash defend against?
questions.explanation: Salts make precomputed tables useless and ensure identical passwords hash differently.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP response header restricts where scripts can load from, helping mitigate XSS?
questions.explanation: A strict Content-Security-Policy blocks inline and untrusted scripts.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command changes a file's permission bits?
questions.explanation: chmod changes mode bits; chown changes ownership.

quizzes.title: Security Fundamentals — Practice
quizzes.description: A self-paced warm-up. Play any time this month; you'll see whether each answer was right straight away.

questions.prompt: Phishing emails most commonly try to…
questions.explanation: Phishing lures you into revealing credentials or running malware.

questions.prompt: Which of these passwords is strongest?
questions.explanation: Length beats complexity: a long passphrase has far more entropy than a short “complex” password.

questions.prompt: What does multi-factor authentication add to a login?
options: A second factor such as an OTP or security key
questions.explanation: MFA requires something you have or are in addition to something you know.

questions.prompt: Which protocol should replace Telnet for remote administration?
questions.explanation: SSH encrypts the session; Telnet sends everything, including passwords, in plaintext.

options: A bug fixed on the day it was found
A flaw with no patch available because the vendor has had zero days to fix it
A virus that deletes itself after a day
questions.explanation: Zero-days are exploited before a fix exists.

questions.prompt: What is the primary job of a firewall?
options: Filter network traffic based on rules
questions.explanation: Firewalls allow or block traffic according to a rule set.
